item.title: openship
item.description:
The Problem The repository provides a self‑hosted deployment platform but declares its runtime dependencies in apps/api/package.json without a lockfile. item.description:
The Problem Mobile developers need a camera UI that goes beyond the basic camera plugin—support for live filters, multi‑camera, barcode scanning, and seamless native performance—without writing platform‑specific code. Integrating those features manually adds native boiler‑plate and fragments the Flutter codebase.

item.title: edgevpn
item.description:

Those solutions introduce a single point of failure, require ongoing license costs, and make it hard to run workloads on edge devices that lack reliable internet connectivity.

item.title: octelium
item.description:
The Problem
Organizations need secure remote access to private infrastructure, but existing tools force a choice: VPNs (broad network access, weak identity controls), ZTNA platforms (complex, commercial), or tunnel services (limited, no identity layer). Teams often end up running multiple tools—a VPN, a reverse proxy, an API gateway—each with separate auth and access policies. Octelium attempts to collapse that stack into one self-hosted platform.

item.title: book to skill
item.description:
The Problem
Technical books are read once, then forgotten. Searching a PDF returns page numbers, not answers. Asking an AI agent about a book either produces hallucinations or a confession that it lacks the content. Manual notes become a 200-line document nobody reopens. The knowledge you paid for sits inert on disk.

item.title: device activity tracker
item.description:

An adversary can infer user behavior simply by measuring the round‑trip time (RTT) of delivery receipts, exposing privacy‑sensitive activity patterns.

item.description:
